option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded mutation points mutant chargen
option.helptext:
How many mutation points a Mutated Human starts character creation with.
Vanilla Caves of Qud gives 12. Caves of Qud Expanded has always given 16, which is the default here.
Set this before creating a character. Changing it has no effect on a character that already exists.

option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded starting skills chargen cooking staunch wounds
option.helptext:
Grants Mutated Humans and True Kin the extra starting skills this mod has always given: Staunch Wounds, Cooking and Gathering, and Meal Preparation. Mutated Humans also get Menacing Stare.
Turn this off to start with exactly vanilla's skills. Vanilla's own starting skills are never removed.
Psionic Adepts are unaffected. Their starting skills are not an addition to a vanilla genotype - they are all the genotype has.
Set this before creating a character.

option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded starting reputation joppa faction chargen
option.helptext:
Gives Mutated Humans {{G|+300}} reputation with Joppa at character creation.
{{y|Off by default}}, unlike the rest of this mod. It grants power with nothing attached to use it, so it is the kind of change you should have to ask for rather than opt out of.
True Kin keep their vanilla Templar standing either way, and Psionic Adepts keep their Mechanimist standing.
Set this before creating a character.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: home base building in Joppa
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded joppa building home base becoming nook
option.helptext:
Adds a walled building near Argyve's workshop in Joppa: a bed, storage, an oven, and a becoming nook with a cybernetics rack.
{{y|Set this before starting a new character.}} Turning it off removes the building the next time you enter Joppa, and the ground beneath it is put back. Turning it back on afterwards does {{r|not}} rebuild it - the building is map data, and once removed from a save it is gone.
Nothing vanilla is removed either way.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: your own Chip Interface slots
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded chip interface slot chargen psionic implant
option.helptext:
Gives your character the Chip Interface slots this mod has always granted: {{G|1}} for a Mutated Human and {{G|2}} for a True Kin. Chips implanted there grant mutations to genotypes that cannot otherwise mutate.
Turn this off to play with a vanilla body and no chip slots at all. Chips can still be found and traded, but you will have nowhere to implant them.
Psionic Adepts are unaffected. Their {{G|4}} slots are the genotype, not an addition to it, and removing them would leave it with nothing.
{{y|Set this before creating a character.}} A body is built once, at character creation, so this cannot change a character who already exists.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Chip Interface slots on other humanoids
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded chip interface npc humanoid anatomy world
option.helptext:
Gives every other humanoid in Qud a Chip Interface slot, as this mod has always done. The slot is merged into the base humanoid anatomy, so it reaches every villager, merchant and snapjaw at once.
Nothing in this mod ever puts a chip in an NPC's slot, so leaving this on has no effect you can see. Turn it off if you would rather other humanoids simply did not have the slot - for instance so that another mod, or a later version of this one, cannot start filling them.
Your own slots are controlled separately, by the option above.
{{y;Set this before creating a character.}} Bodies are built once, when a creature is generated, so this cannot change humanoids that already exist in a save.

option.DisplayText: {{C|Qud Expanded}}: Two-Gun Stance in Multiweapon Fighting
option.SearchKeywords: qud expanded akimbo multiweapon pistol dual wield skill
option.helptext:
Adds {{W|Two-Gun Stance}} to the Multiweapon Fighting tree, letting a dual-wielder fire both pistols at once without buying into the Pistol tree.
It is the same ability as {{W|Akimbo}}, which the Pistol tree already grants, and it is the only ranged power in a tree that is otherwise entirely melee - every other Multiweapon power raises your melee offhand hit chance. Buying it in both trees gains you nothing.
Turn this off to leave Multiweapon Fighting exactly as vanilla has it. Akimbo in the Pistol tree is untouched either way.
